title: Move Commerce trade offices to the U.S. Trade Representative
proposal: The next President should consider moving the International Trade Administration and parts of the Bureau of Industry and Security to USTR, along with other trade agencies like the Export-Import Bank, and ask whether some should exist at all.
quote: The International Trade Administration (ITA) and parts of the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) should be streamlined and moved to the Office

title: Consolidate or abolish the Economic Development Administration
proposal: EDA grant programs should be consolidated with other programs or eliminated. The chapter later says abolishing EDA and moving its funding to similar grant programs would be more efficient.
quote: federal economic development grant programs, should be consolidated with other programs and/or eliminated;

title: Merge federal statistical agencies into one
proposal: The Bureau of Economic Analysis, Census Bureau, and the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics should be combined into one statistical agency, or at least studied for merger.
quote: The Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau, as well as the Department of Labor’s Bureau of Labor Statistics, should be consolidated

title: Make the Patent and Trademark Office a performance-based organization
proposal: The President should consider making USPTO a performance-based organization under the Office of Management and Budget.
quote: The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) should be made into a performance-based organization under the Office of Management and Budget (OMB);

title: Combine the patent office and NIST into one agency
proposal: As an alternative, USPTO could be merged with NIST into a new Office of Patents, Trademarks, and Standards, with non-essential research cut or moved.
quote: the USPTO should be consolidated with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in a new U.S. Office of Patents, Trademarks, and Standards,

title: Break up and downsize NOAA
proposal: NOAA should be dismantled, with many functions eliminated, moved to other agencies, privatized, or given to states and territories.
quote: The National Oceanographic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) should be dismantled and many of its functions eliminated, sent to other agencies, privatized,

title: Staff the Commerce Secretary's office with political appointees
proposal: The new administration should fully staff the Office of the Secretary with political appointees, send detailees back to their bureaus on Day One, and seek more direct funding and appointee positions.
quote: fully staff OS with political appointees, send all existing detailees back to their home bureaus on Day One,

title: Put political appointees over Commerce budget offices
proposal: Political leaders should be installed right away in the CFO and administration offices, and appointees should join career staff in all budget talks with OMB and Congress.
quote: political appointees receive a mandate to communicate with external partners alongside career staff at every stage of the budget

title: Abolish non-required Commerce advisory committees
proposal: Commerce advisory committees should be reviewed, abolished if not required by law, and the rest reconstituted.
quote: all such committees should be reviewed regarding whether they are required by statute and abolished if they are not.

title: Quickly fill ITA leadership posts with appointees
proposal: The administration should fill International Trade Administration Assistant Secretary and Deputy Assistant Secretary jobs with appointees as fast as possible.
quote: Strong political leadership is needed in ITA’s policymaking positions from

title: Restore in-person trade verifications, especially in China
proposal: Commerce should restart and expand in-person verifications in trade cases that were paused during the pandemic, especially for China.
quote: Re-establish and expand suspended in-person pandemic-related verifications, particularly regarding the People’s Republic of China.

title: Use AI to detect trade duty evasion
proposal: Commerce should use advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to find duty circumvention and cases to start on its own.
quote: Implement advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to identify opportunities for self-initiation, detect circumvention, and prevent bad actors from gaming the system.

title: Pursue unpaid trade duties more aggressively
proposal: Commerce should work with Customs, Justice, and Treasury to aggressively collect unpaid duties from importers.
quote: aggressively pursue importers of record and other beneficiaries for unpaid duties,

title: Require large deposits or U.S. assets from foreign importers
proposal: Foreign importers of goods subject to antidumping or countervailing duties should have to pay large cash deposits, register U.S. assets, or be barred from importing those goods.
quote: require foreign importers of record (IORs) to make cash deposits far in excess of established duty rates

title: Audit trade enforcement office for regulatory capture
proposal: Commerce should conduct a regulatory capture audit and add guardrails against improper bureaucratic actions.
quote: Conduct a regulatory capture audit and put guardrails in place to address improper exercise of bureaucratic prerogative.

title: Stop favoring foreign firms in trade duty cases
proposal: Commerce should end the practice of giving foreign companies the benefit of the doubt over U.S. companies in antidumping and countervailing duty cases.
quote: Reverse the practice of giving the benefit of the doubt to foreign companies versus U.S. companies in AD/CVD proceedings.

title: Set policy for big U.S. investors facing trade duty petitions
proposal: Commerce should set a policy for companies that invest heavily in the U.S. and therefore import a lot and face duty petitions.
quote: Establish a policy for addressing companies that invest heavily in the U.S. and thus have large import volumes, exposing them to AD/CVD petitions.

title: Let Commerce start trade cases when industry cannot
proposal: Commerce should set a fair process to start antidumping and countervailing duty cases on its own when industry lacks resources.
quote: Establish an effective, fair, and objective process for self-initiation of AD/CVD proceedings when industry lacks the resources or ability to act.

title: Revive the China-specific trade enforcement unit
proposal: Commerce should bring back its China-specific non-market economy unit.
quote: Revive the China-specific non-market economy unit.

title: Make the surrogate country list process transparent
proposal: Commerce should make the process for choosing surrogate countries in trade cases transparent.
quote: Provide transparency in the surrogate country list development process.

title: New method for pricing Chinese goods in dumping cases
proposal: Commerce should create a new way to set normal values in Chinese antidumping cases, since no country is comparable to China.
quote: Develop a new methodology to determine normal values in Chinese anti-dumping cases because

title: Restructure Commerce analysts to track supply chains
proposal: Industry and Analysis should be restructured to analyze supply chains on an ongoing basis, with standing teams on decoupling from China, the defense industrial base, critical supply chains, and emerging tech.
quote: I&A should be permanently restructured to perform supply-chain analysis on an ongoing basis for the U.S. government,

title: Replace Top Market Reports with competitiveness studies
proposal: Industry and Analysis Top Market Reports should be replaced by competitiveness assessments of critical sectors.
quote: could be better replaced by industry competitiveness assessments in critical sectors of the economy.

title: Rethink overseas Commercial Service posts
proposal: The Commercial Service should rank posts by set priorities, expand shared "partner posts," decide which posts are justified, and have State pay more for posts it considers vital.
quote: If the State Department deems the diplomatic value of a permanent in-country CS post to be vital to the national interest, then State should bear more of the cost

title: Combine the Advocacy Center and SelectUSA
proposal: Global Markets should merge and elevate the Advocacy Center and SelectUSA into an office led by a Deputy Assistant Secretary, and seek authority to use it to encourage reshoring.
quote: Global Markets should also consolidate and elevate the Advocacy Center and SelectUSA as relatively low-cost tools to drive large-scale export transactions

title: Reverse 2008-2016 export control loosening
proposal: Export control reforms from 2008 to 2016 that loosened rules on dual-use exports should be reversed, and rules for countries of concern like China and Russia tightened.
quote: Those reforms still present in the Department of Commerce’s EAR must be reversed.

title: Use export controls to protect data and move production out of China
proposal: Export controls should be used to prevent theft of personal information and to encourage U.S. companies to move production out of China.
quote: U.S. export control regulations should be utilized to prevent theft of personally identifiable information and to encourage U.S. companies to shift production out of China

title: Open process to nominate technologies for export controls
proposal: BIS should let anyone nominate emerging and foundational technologies for export control, publish nominations quarterly for comment, explain decisions, and allow challenges.
quote: BIS should create an open, transparent rulemaking process by which any industry participant, private entity, or branch of the government may, at any time, submit nominations

title: Change how export license disputes are decided
proposal: The BIS Under Secretary should lead license dispute resolution, each agency should get an equal vote, and unresolved disputes should go to the National Security Advisor and Cabinet secretaries.
quote: BIS’s authority to overrule other agency votes should be changed. Each agency should have one equal vote and, if a licensing dispute remains

title: Give Congress quarterly export data
proposal: BIS should give congressional committees quarterly export data, including exporters, products, destinations, and license decisions.
quote: BIS should provide specific congressional committees with data from the Automated Export System on a quarterly basis.

title: Deny export licenses to countries that block end-use checks
proposal: BIS should deny export licenses to countries, such as China and Russia, that do not allow adequate U.S. end-use checks.
quote: BIS must deny export licenses to countries that do not permit adequate end-use checks (e.g., China/Russia) by

title: Train export enforcement officers in forensic audits
proposal: BIS should strengthen the forensic audit skills of its export enforcement officers through more frequent training.
quote: BIS should also strengthen the forensic audit capabilities of its

title: Close export licensing loopholes for countries of concern
proposal: Export rules for countries of concern should remove the "specially designed" loophole and eliminate license exceptions, including for technology shared through standards bodies.
quote: Eliminating the “specially designed” licensing loophole;

title: Move China and Russia to stricter export license groups
proposal: China and Russia should be moved into more restrictive export licensing country groups (D or E).
quote: Redesignating China and Russia to more highly prohibitive export licensing groups (country groups D or E);

title: Broaden foreign direct product rules
proposal: Export rules covering foreign-made items built with U.S. technology should be broadened.
quote: Broadening foreign direct product rules;

title: Lower the de minimis threshold for export controls
proposal: The share of U.S. content that triggers export controls should drop from 25 percent to 10 percent, or 0 percent for critical technologies.
quote: Reducing the de minimis threshold from 25 percent to 10 percent—or 0 percent for critical technologies;

title: Tighten deemed export rules for foreign nationals
proposal: Deemed export rules should be tightened to stop technology transfer to foreign nationals from countries of concern.
quote: Tightening the deemed export rules to prevent technology transfer to foreign nationals from countries of concern;

title: Narrow the "fundamental research" export exemption
proposal: The definition of "fundamental research" should be tightened to address exploitation of U.S. universities through funding, students, researchers, and recruitment.
quote: Tightening the definition of “fundamental research” to address exploitation of the open U.S. university system by authoritarian governments

title: Restrict all exports to countries of concern
proposal: If a Cold War with China has begun, exports of goods, software, and technology to countries of concern should be banned or controlled unless there is good cause, such as humanitarian aid.
quote: any exports of goods, software, and technology to countries of concern, whether directly or indirectly, should be prohibited or controlled in the absence of good cause

title: Add more Chinese and Russian firms to the Entity List
proposal: BIS should add more entities to the Entity List and apply a "policy of denial" to exports to them.
quote: BIS must add more entities to the Entity List and apply a license review “policy of denial” that prohibits exports to these entities.

title: Penalize Entity List firms that violate export controls
proposal: Entity List companies that break export controls should lose export privileges through the Denied Persons List and, if serious, face Treasury sanctions.
quote: Entity List parties that violate export controls should be placed on the BIS Denied Persons List (and thereby lose export privileges)

title: Executive order restricting exports of Americans' data
proposal: Commerce should draft an executive order under emergency economic powers law to control exports of U.S. persons' data to countries of concern, implemented by BIS rules.
quote: draft and implement an executive order (EO) based on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, which expands export control authority

title: Put TikTok and WeChat on the Entity List
proposal: BIS should add app providers like WeChat and ByteDance/TikTok to the Entity List, which would block updates and make the apps stop working in the U.S.
quote: BIS should additionally designate app providers (such as WeChat and Byte Dance/TikTok) known for undermining U.S. national security

title: Commercialize National Weather Service forecasting
proposal: The National Weather Service should focus on gathering data and fully commercialize its forecasting.
quote: Because private companies rely on these data, the NWS should fully commercialize its forecasting operations.

title: Use commercial partners for weather technology
proposal: NOAA should prioritize commercial partnerships for weather technology to get cost-efficient research and data.
quote: Commercialization of weather technologies should be prioritized to ensure that taxpayer dollars are invested in the most

title: Make the Weather Service a performance-based organization
proposal: The National Weather Service should be considered for becoming a performance-based organization focused on delivering accurate data.
quote: The NWS should be a candidate to become a Performance-Based Organization

title: Review Hurricane Center and satellite data; present climate data neutrally
proposal: The work of the National Hurricane Center and satellite data service should be reviewed, and climate data should be presented without adjustments favoring either side.
quote: Data collected by the department should be presented neutrally, without adjustments intended to support any one side in the climate debate.

title: Move ocean survey work to Coast Guard and USGS
proposal: National Ocean Service survey functions should move to the U.S. Coast Guard and U.S. Geological Survey.
quote: These functions could be transferred to the U.S. Coast Guard and U.S. Geological Survey to increase efficiency.

title: Streamline NOAA Fisheries and Fish and Wildlife Service
proposal: The goals of the National Marine Fisheries Service and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service should be streamlined to reduce overlap.
quote: Streamline NMFS. Overlap exists between the National Marine Fisheries Service and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

title: Align marine sanctuaries with fisheries law
proposal: The Magnuson-Stevens fisheries law and the National Marine Sanctuaries Act should be harmonized, and sanctuary expansion reviewed, since no-fishing zones can conflict with fisheries management.
quote: Harmonize the Magnuson–Stevens Act with the National Marine Sanctuaries Act.

title: Withdraw the 30x30 conservation executive order
proposal: The 30x30 executive order and America the Beautiful initiative, which the chapter says close ocean areas to fishing while advancing offshore wind, should be withdrawn.
quote: Withdraw the 30x30 Executive Order and Associated America the Beautiful

title: Change marine mammal and endangered species regulations
proposal: Regulations under the Marine Mammal Protection Act and Endangered Species Act should be modified, which the chapter says burden fisheries and Native subsistence.
quote: Modify Regulations Implementing the Marine Mammal Protection Act and the Endangered Species Act.

title: Exempt fisheries actions from NEPA reviews
proposal: Fisheries actions should get a NEPA exemption, with Commerce and the Council on Environmental Quality working to reduce repeated reviews.
quote: The Department of Commerce and the Council on Environmental Quality should collaborate to reduce this redundancy.

title: Downsize NOAA research and end most climate research
proposal: Most of the climate change research in NOAA's Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research should be disbanded, and its labs reviewed for consolidation.
quote: The preponderance of its climate-change research should be disbanded.

title: Break up NOAA's ship and aircraft office
proposal: NOAA's Office of Marine and Aviation Operations should be broken up and its ships and planes reassigned to GSA or other agencies.
quote: The Office of Marine and Aviation Operations, which provides the ships and planes used by NOAA agencies, should be broken up

title: Use prizes and competitions for NOAA research
proposal: NOAA should use small innovation prizes and competitions to attract startups and small businesses.
quote: Multiple competitions should take place in cities to attract a variety of innovators and investors to propel innovation forward

title: Move the Office of Space Commerce to the Secretary's office
proposal: The Office of Space Commerce should be moved from NOAA's satellite service back to the Office of the Secretary.
quote: The Office needs to be returned to OS, within which it existed for the first two decades of its existence.

title: Create a government-wide commercial space licensing policy
proposal: The President should direct by executive order the Office of Space Commerce and National Space Council to set a whole-of-government policy for licensing and overseeing commercial space.
quote: The President should, by executive order, direct the Office of Space Commerce, working with the National Space Council, to establish a whole-of-government policy

title: Add political appointee positions at the Census Bureau
proposal: OPM should give the Census Bureau more political appointee positions, filled early, to guide the 2030 census.
quote: This will require the Office of Personnel Management to allocate additional political appointee positions to the Census Bureau.

title: Review Census Bureau IT and management spending
proposal: The new administration should immediately review Census Bureau financial, IT, and HR systems to control costs and fix failed investments.
quote: The new Administration must immediately conduct a review to identify ways to better control costs and reverse recent failures of investments

title: Audit the 2030 census cost estimate
proposal: The administration should immediately audit the 2030 census lifecycle cost estimate and redo it if needed.
quote: An incoming Administration should immediately audit the lifecycle cost estimate (LCCE) for the 2030 census and conduct a new LCCE if necessary.

title: Cut duplication in census operations
proposal: The 2030 census plan should eliminate duplication between ongoing surveys and decennial operations.
quote: ensure the decennial operational plan eliminates current duplication among ongoing census operations

title: Engage conservative groups to boost census response
proposal: The census partnership program should be reviewed, and the administration should engage conservative groups to encourage census participation.
quote: A new Administration should work to actively engage with conservative groups and voices to promote response to the decennial census.

title: Add a citizenship question to the census
proposal: The administration should include a citizenship question in the decennial census.
quote: Any successful conservative Administration must include a citizenship question in the census.

title: Review planned changes to census race and ethnicity questions
proposal: The administration should take control of and review proposed changes combining race and ethnicity questions, working with OMB.
quote: A new conservative Administration should take control of this process and thoroughly review any changes.

title: Remove intrusive or less useful census questions
proposal: All decennial census questions should be reevaluated, with intrusive or less crucial questions moved to another survey or removed.
quote: Overly intrusive questions or less crucial data should either be moved to another survey or removed from Census programs entirely.

title: Review American Community Survey questions
proposal: Each American Community Survey question should be reviewed to make sure it is useful and not overly intrusive.
quote: each question should be carefully reviewed to ensure the data are useful and that the questions are not overly intrusive.

title: Review the Economic Census for intrusiveness
proposal: The Economic Census should be examined so it is not overly intrusive, and supplemented with industry and other federal data where possible.
quote: it should be carefully examined to ensure the Economic Census is not overly intrusive.

title: Review the Supplemental Poverty Measure
proposal: The Census Bureau should review whether the Supplemental Poverty Measure is accurate.
quote: The Census Bureau should review the Supplemental Poverty Measure (SPM) to consider whether it provides an accurate measure

title: Abolish Census Bureau advisory committees
proposal: The Census Bureau's National Advisory Committee on Racial, Ethnic, and Other Populations should be abolished, and other non-required committees reevaluated or abolished.
quote: The NAC should immediately be abolished by the incoming Administration.

title: Centralize EDA grant decisions
proposal: If EDA is not abolished, its decision-making should move to the Assistant Secretary's office so funding aligns with administration priorities.
quote: Consolidation of decision-making to the Assistant Secretary’s office to better align funding with conservative political purposes.

title: Build on Opportunity Zones
proposal: EDA should build on the Opportunity Zones program for investment in distressed communities.
quote: Building on the initial success of Opportunity Zones, which incentivized over $75 billion in private sector investment in distressed communities

title: Refocus the Minority Business Development Agency
proposal: MBDA should focus on policy analysis about free markets, socialism, and the effects of taxes and regulation, and act as a research clearinghouse.
quote: Conducting policy analysis on the benefit of free markets, the evils of socialism and Communism, and the destructive effect of taxes and regulations on minority businesses;

title: Tighten oversight of MBDA business centers
proposal: MBDA business centers should have strict funding oversight, clear success measures, and consequences for poor performance.
quote: Ensuring MBDA business centers operate efficiently with strict oversight of funding, clear metrics for success, and consequences for poor performance;

title: Back allied candidates to lead the world IP organization
proposal: The administration should support like-minded countries' candidates for World Intellectual Property Organization leadership.
quote: Support like-minded countries as candidates for leadership in the World Intellectual Property Organization

title: Revisit patent eligibility rules
proposal: The administration should re-examine patent eligibility under Section 101 of the Patent Act and support reforms for emerging technologies like AI and quantum computing.
quote: Re-examine patent eligibility requirements in Section 101 of the Patent Act

title: Speed up Patent Trial and Appeal Board processing
proposal: The administration should take a balanced approach to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board and process applications and appeals quickly and openly.
quote: Take a balanced approach to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board and prioritize rapid and transparent processing of applications and appeals.

title: Crack down on trademark counterfeiters
proposal: The administration should work with Congress and other agencies to find and punish trademark infringers and counterfeiters.
quote: Work with Administration partners and Congress to find and punish trademark infringers and counterfeiters.

title: Oppose patent waivers for COVID-19 vaccines and new technology
proposal: The administration should oppose intellectual property waivers for cutting-edge technologies, including COVID-19 vaccines, through the World Trade Organization.
quote: Oppose efforts to provide intellectual property waivers for cutting-edge technologies, including for COVID-19 vaccines and therapeutics,

title: Consolidate federal civilian research
proposal: The administration should evaluate and consolidate federal civilian research so it serves the national interest.
quote: An incoming Administration should evaluate the federal government’s civilian research footprint and consolidate those functions

title: Privatize the Manufacturing Extension Partnership
proposal: The administration should propose legislation to end the $150 million Hollings Manufacturing Extension Partnership and fully privatize its centers.
quote: The next Administration should propose legislation to zero out this $150 million program and fully privatize existing MEP centers.

title: Hand the Baldrige program to a private foundation
proposal: The Baldrige Performance Excellence Program should be fully handed to the Baldrige Award Foundation and run by non-government staff through fees.
quote: Maintenance and operation of the program should be entirely handed over to the Baldridge Award Foundation to be run by non-government staff via fees.

title: Revive NIST technology transfer initiatives
proposal: NIST should restart Trump-era Technology Transfer and return-on-investment initiatives to speed commercialization of federally funded science.
quote: NIST should reinvigorate the Technology Transfer and ROI (return on investment) initiatives begun under the Trump Administration.

title: Boost U.S. role in standards bodies and exclude China
proposal: NIST should encourage more U.S. participation in international standards bodies and the exclusion of adversaries like China.
quote: NIST should explore ways to incentivize broader U.S. participation in standards-setting bodies and the exclusion of participants from adversaries like China.

title: Move NTIS functions into NIST
proposal: The National Technical Information Service's functions should move to NIST and merge with technology transfer work.
quote: NTIS’s functions should be moved to NIST and consolidated with the Tech Transfer and ROI initiatives.

title: Review online free speech policy and big tech censorship
proposal: NTIA should immediately review federal policy on online free speech and propose solutions to big tech censorship.
quote: Immediately conduct a thorough review of federal policy regarding free speech online and provide policy solutions to address big tech’s censorship of speech.

title: Fully implement the ICTS supply chain security order
proposal: NTIA should fully implement Trump-era executive order authorities on information and communications technology supply chain security.
quote: Fully implement the Trump Administration’s Information and Communications Technology and Services (ICTS) Executive Order authorities

title: Lease unused federal spectrum
proposal: NTIA should begin short-term leasing of government spectrum while keeping agency use rights.
quote: Begin short term, temporary leasing of government allocated spectrum to ensure optimum utilization while preserving federal agency use rights.

title: Advocate FCC licensing that supports commercial space
proposal: NTIA should push for FCC licensing decisions that keep U.S. leadership in commercial space.
quote: Advocate for licensing decisions at the Federal Communications Commission that continue to enable U.S. dominance in the commercial space industry.

title: Strengthen U.S. role at the International Telecommunication Union
proposal: NTIA should work with the U.S. delegation to the International Telecommunication Union to win adoption of U.S. positions on spectrum.
quote: NTIA should work with the U.S. delegation to ensure maximum adoption of the U.S. position.

title: Reset priorities for broadband grants
proposal: NTIA should reevaluate broadband grants and set administration priorities, with 5G infrastructure in rural and exurban areas first.
quote: Reevaluate broadband grant programs and, when possible, establish Administration priorities in how each grant is structured.

title: Review the FirstNet public safety network
proposal: NTIA should evaluate FirstNet's performance and long-term value given newer technologies.
quote: Evaluate the performance and long-term value proposition of FirstNet in view of modern technologies that will render it obsolete.
